title: General Science Test 2 (Biology & Everyday Science — most probable)

questions.q: Which organelle is known as the 'powerhouse of the cell'?
questions.explain: Mitochondria produce Adenosine Triphosphate (ATP), the energy currency of the cell, through respiration.

questions.q: Photosynthesis in a plant cell takes place in the:
questions.explain: Chloroplasts contain the green pigment chlorophyll, which traps sunlight for photosynthesis.

questions.q: Protein synthesis in the cell is carried out by the:
questions.explain: Ribosomes assemble proteins; lysosomes are the cell's digestive ('suicide') bags.

questions.q: The part of the cell that controls all its activities and contains Deoxyribonucleic Acid (DNA) is the:
questions.explain: The nucleus holds the genetic material (Deoxyribonucleic Acid (DNA)) and acts as the control centre of the cell.

questions.q: Photosynthesis releases which gas into the atmosphere?
questions.explain: Plants take in CO₂ and water and, using sunlight, produce glucose and release oxygen: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂.

questions.q: How many chambers does the human heart have?
questions.explain: Two upper atria and two lower ventricles — this keeps oxygenated and deoxygenated blood separate.

questions.q: The largest organ of the human body is the:
questions.explain: The skin is the largest organ; the liver is the largest internal gland.

questions.q: The longest and strongest bone in the human body is the:
questions.explain: The femur bears the body's weight; the smallest bone is the stapes in the ear.

questions.q: An adult human skeleton has how many bones?
questions.explain: Babies are born with about 300 bones; many fuse together, leaving 206 in adults.

questions.q: Which blood group is called the 'universal donor'?
questions.explain: O negative blood has no A, B or Rh antigens, so it can be given to anyone in an emergency.

questions.q: Which blood group is called the 'universal recipient'?
questions.explain: AB positive people can receive blood of any group because their blood has no anti-A/anti-B antibodies.

questions.q: Haemoglobin, which carries oxygen in the blood, contains the mineral:
questions.explain: Iron deficiency lowers haemoglobin and causes anaemia; haemoglobin gives blood its red colour.

questions.q: Which blood cells protect the body by fighting germs and infections?
questions.explain: WBCs are the soldiers of the blood; RBCs carry oxygen and platelets help in clotting.

questions.q: Blood clotting, which stops bleeding from a wound, is the function of:
questions.explain: Platelets release substances that form a clot; Vitamin K is also needed for clotting.

questions.q: Insulin, the hormone that controls blood sugar, is secreted by the:
questions.explain: Deficiency of insulin causes diabetes mellitus, in which blood sugar rises.

questions.q: Diabetes mellitus is caused by the deficiency of:
questions.explain: Without enough insulin, glucose cannot enter cells properly and blood sugar stays high.

questions.q: The 'emergency hormone', released during fear, anger or stress, is:
questions.explain: Adrenaline from the adrenal glands speeds up heartbeat and prepares the body for 'fight or flight'.

questions.q: The structural and functional unit of the kidney is the:
questions.explain: Each kidney has about a million nephrons that filter blood and form urine.

questions.q: The basic unit of the nervous system is the:
questions.explain: Neurons carry electrical messages; the nephron is the kidney's unit — the pair is a common trap.

questions.q: The largest part of the human brain, responsible for thinking and memory, is the:
questions.explain: The cerebrum is the biggest part; the cerebellum coordinates balance and the medulla controls breathing and heartbeat.

questions.q: Night blindness is caused by the deficiency of:
questions.explain: Vitamin A is needed for the retina's light-sensitive pigment; rich sources are carrot, papaya, mango and milk.

questions.q: Scurvy, a disease of bleeding gums, is caused by the deficiency of:
questions.explain: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is abundant in citrus fruits like amla, lemon and orange.

questions.q: Rickets, in which children's bones become soft and bend, is caused by the deficiency of:
questions.explain: Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium; sunlight is its natural source.

questions.q: Beriberi is caused by the deficiency of:
questions.explain: Beriberi affects the nerves and muscles; thiamine is found in whole grains and pulses.

questions.q: Which vitamin is essential for the clotting of blood?
questions.explain: Vitamin K helps the liver produce clotting factors; newborns are often given a Vitamin K dose.

questions.q: Anaemia (low haemoglobin) is most commonly caused by the deficiency of:
questions.explain: Iron is needed to make haemoglobin; its deficiency causes weakness and paleness.

questions.q: The mineral most essential for strong bones and teeth is:
questions.explain: Calcium with Vitamin D keeps bones strong; milk and ragi are good sources.

questions.q: Goitre, the swelling of the thyroid gland in the neck, is caused by the deficiency of:
questions.explain: Iodised salt prevents goitre; iodine is needed to make the thyroxine hormone.

questions.q: Malaria is caused by a protozoan parasite named:
questions.explain: Plasmodium enters the body through the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito.

questions.q: Malaria is spread by the bite of the female:
questions.explain: Anopheles spreads malaria (night biter); Aedes aegypti spreads dengue (day biter) — the pair repeats in exams.

questions.q: Dengue fever is transmitted by the mosquito:
questions.explain: Aedes aegypti breeds in clean stored water and bites during the day.

questions.q: Tuberculosis (TB) is caused by a:
questions.explain: Tuberculosis (TB) is a bacterial disease (Mycobacterium tuberculosis) spread through the air; the Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) vaccine protects against it.

questions.q: Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome (AIDS) is caused by the:
questions.explain: Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) attacks the immune system; it spreads through infected blood and needles, not by touch or sharing food.

questions.q: Rabies, a fatal disease of the nervous system, is usually transmitted by:
questions.explain: Rabies is a viral disease; washing the wound and taking the anti-rabies vaccine promptly saves life.

questions.q: Cholera, a severe water-borne disease, is caused by a:
questions.explain: Cholera spreads through contaminated water and causes rapid dehydration; Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) is the life-saving treatment.

questions.q: Typhoid fever is caused by the bacterium:
questions.explain: Typhoid spreads through contaminated food and water; the Widal test is used in its diagnosis.

questions.q: Which nutrient provides the maximum energy per gram to the body?
questions.explain: Fats give about 9 kcal per gram, more than double the energy from carbohydrates or proteins (about 4 kcal/g).

questions.q: Penicillin, the first widely used antibiotic, was discovered by:
questions.explain: Fleming noticed in 1928 that a mould (Penicillium) killed bacteria around it.

questions.q: The first vaccine in history, against smallpox, was developed by:
questions.explain: Jenner used cowpox material in 1796; smallpox was finally eradicated from the world in 1980.

questions.q: Proteins are called the 'body-building foods' because they are mainly needed for:
options: Growth and repair of body tissues
questions.explain: Proteins build muscles and repair wear and tear; pulses, milk, egg and soyabean are rich sources.
